title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading the northern Rhône and eating with it
objectives: Pair Syrah and Viognier with food

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels name the appellation, like Côte-Rôtie or Crozes-Hermitage, the producer and sometimes a lieu-dit, a named vineyard. Grapes aren't usually named, but every red is Syrah. Négociants like Guigal, Chapoutier and Jaboulet are important, alongside small domaines.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Northern Rhône Syrah suits lamb with herbs and black pepper, game, duck and grilled beef; its pepper echoes peppercorn sauces. Condrieu suits lobster, crab and dishes with apricot or mild spice. White Hermitage suits rich fish and truffles. Serve reds at 16 to 18 degrees; decant young Hermitage and Cornas.

steps.prompt: Which dish suits a Cornas or Hermitage?
steps.explanation: Rich game and pepper suit Syrah's power and spice.

steps.body: Crozes-Hermitage and Saint-Joseph from good producers offer a taste of northern Rhône Syrah at a fraction of Hermitage prices.

steps.prompt: Great Hermitage can age for decades.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels name the appellation; reds are Syrah
Syrah suits lamb, game and peppercorn sauce
Hermitage and Cornas benefit from decanting and age
